newsitem.title: UK: Bluebird sets terms of share repurchase.
newsitem.headline: Bluebird sets terms of share repurchase.

text.p: British toymaker Bluebird Toys Plc said on Monday it would start an operation on Tuesday to buy back up to 3.0 million of its shares, using SBC Warburg as its agent.

In a statement, Bluebird said the repurchase followed a general authority granted at its agm on May 22 this year. "The company has now decided to implement such a share purchase programme, subject to market conditions."
"The purchase is designed to achieve a more efficient capital structure for the long term and to enhance earnings per share and shareholder value," it added.
Bluebird said it had appointed SBC Warburg as its agent to make market puchases "with effect from October 1, 1996".
"Where purchases are made by SBC Warburg acting as agent, the price paid by the company in excess of 27.68p per share will be a distribution for tax purposes.
"Certain shareholders may be in a position to reclaim part or all of the associated tax credit equal to 25 percent of the distribution," the company said.
Based on (Monday's) closing price of 140.5p the distribution element of the purchase would be equal to about 112.8p per share with an associated tax credit of some 28.2p per share, it added.
